title: Zero-Energy Problems for Supersymmetric Hamiltonians on a Chain Are $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-Complete
abstract: We study exact zero modes of supersymmetric quantum systems whose interactions are arranged on a one-dimensional chain. For Hermitian supercharges, deciding whether a zero mode exists is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete, and the hard instances are geometrically local on a chain. We also classify an explicitly encoded nilpotent $\mathcal{N}=2$ formulation: its exact-zero problem is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete, including the restriction in which the associated Hamiltonian is local on a chain. Both classifications use a verification theorem for simultaneous sparse linear constraints and the same one-dimensional frustration-free Hamiltonian construction. The construction gives an explicit inverse-polynomial lower bound on the ground energy of every reduced NO instance, separating it from zero.
summary: This work establishes that determining if a supersymmetric quantum Hamiltonian on a 1D chain has a zero-energy ground state is QMA1-complete. The authors achieve this by constructing a rigorous reduction from the Quantum Satisfiability problem. This result places the problem of finding exact zero modes within the realm of computationally hard problems, linking condensed matter physics to quantum computation theory.
main_problem: The paper determines the computational complexity of deciding whether a supersymmetric quantum Hamiltonian on a chain possesses an exact zero-energy ground state.
main_result: The zero-energy problem for both Hermitian and nilpotent supersymmetric Hamiltonians on a chain is proven to be QMA1-complete.
method: The proof involves a polynomial-time reduction from the Quantum Satisfiability problem (QSAT) on a line of sites, preserving the spectral gap structure.
model_or_system: The study focuses on supersymmetric quantum systems whose interactions are restricted to a one-dimensional chain. The Hamiltonians are constructed using supercharges ($H=Q^2$ or $H=\{Q, Q^\dagger\}$) acting on fermionic modes.
key_observables: Zero energy (ground state energy), spectral gap, and the existence of zero modes.
important_parameters: Geometric locality, the size of the chain, and the polynomial bounds derived from the reduction.
main_assumptions: The reduction relies on the existence of a polynomial-time, uniform reduction from QSAT and the ability to maintain gap structure across Hamiltonian constructions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the complexity by first defining the physical models (supersymmetric Hamiltonians) and then constructing a rigorous, gap-preserving reduction from a known QMA1-complete problem (QSAT) to the zero-energy problem on the chain.
why_interesting: It provides a deep connection between fundamental concepts in quantum many-body physics (supersymmetry, ground state properties) and the computational complexity class QMA1, suggesting that finding exact ground states in these systems is computationally hard.
